A raw secret value wrapped over several lines passes test 7. leaks() checks the raw form only against the log text as printed (lab.mjs line 477, text.includes(value)), while the base64 and hex forms are also searched in a whitespace-stripped copy (joined) and in the hex stream. Reproduced, each an added build-job step with PW mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD: printf '%s' "$PW" | fold -w 10 passes 26/26 (ci-raw-fold); echo "$PW" | fold -w 16 passes 26/26 (ci-raw-fold-echo); echoing ${PW:0:12} and ${PW:12} on two lines passes 26/26 (ci-raw-two-halves). Each prints the whole value, readable, in the step output. README line 119 tells the learner "Test 7 finds a value as written, in base64 or in hex, even wrapped", and the loop-5 reconciliation for ops-sme-r5-06 specified that test 7 detects "the raw, base64 and hex forms across line wrapping"; the raw form is the one that is not. On a runner, GitHub's redaction "largely relies on finding an exact match for the specific secret value" (secure-use reference), so a wrapped value is not masked. Like the xxd shapes closed in loop 5, the shape is off the README path, so this is a false accept of a real leak in a form the README says is detected, not a learner-path false accept. Related, not filed as a defect: hexdump -C of the value passes 26/26 (its offset has no colon and its text column shows the value in 16-character pieces), which ops-edu-r5-05 places under the README limit, although README line 119 says "in hex" without naming the layouts.

evidence.section: Use secrets for sensitive information (redaction relies on an exact match)
Use secrets for sensitive information (automatic redaction is not guaranteed)

findings.recommendation: In leaks(), also report the raw form when the whitespace-stripped log contains it (for example: if (text.includes(value) || joined.includes(value)) return { name, how: '' }). The made-up value has no whitespace, so this cannot flag ordinary output. Recheck: ci-raw-fold, ci-raw-fold-echo and ci-raw-two-halves fail only test 7 with the existing message; S11-S14, the add-mask-of-derived form and the hex-looking ordinary output still pass; both summaries are unchanged. Optionally qualify README line 119 to the layouts detected ("in hex as xxd prints it"), or let hexStream also read hexdump -C lines (an offset followed by two spaces, a |text| column).

When an exception escapes before the shop call, tests 24-26 name it but keep the no-call advice, which contradicts the code the learner wrote. With httpx.Timeout(connect=2.0, read=3.0) written inside the handler (the most literal reading of README phase 4 rule 2), test 24 says "got 500 (an exception escaped unhandled: ValueError: httpx.Timeout must either include a default, or set all four parameters explicitly.) and the service made no HTTPX call to the shop api, so its limits could not be checked: call the api with httpx, as the starter does"; test 25 ends "make the call and send the caller's token on it" and test 26 "make the call to the shop api with httpx" (lab.mjs lines 241, 255, 276). The learner already calls the api with httpx; the error comes from building the Timeout. The loop-5 required change for ops-sme-r5-03 and ops-edu-r5-02 part 1 was to report the exception instead of the no-call message, with the no-call wording kept only for code that made no HTTPX request and raised nothing. Second, new in loop 6: when the app has a catch-all Exception or 500 handler, service_behavior.py (lines 89-93) reruns the request with a non-raising client and records only the status, dropping the exception it already caught. With a catch-all handler that maps timeouts and refusals correctly and the same inline Timeout, tests 24-26 say "got 500 and the service made no HTTPX call to the shop api ... call the api with httpx, as the starter does", with no exception named (svc-catchall-plus-inline-valueerror). Starlette's ServerErrorMiddleware always re-raises after an installed 500 handler, which is why the fallback exists; the fallback itself is sound, and correct catch-all, typed-handler and middleware mappings pass 26/26.

evidence.section: ServerErrorMiddleware.__call__: re-raise after the installed 500 handler (lines 183-186)

In the catch-all fallback, keep error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}" (and the handler's status) so lab.mjs can name it. Recheck: svc-inline-timeout-ctor-valueerror and svc-catchall-plus-inline-valueerror both name the ValueError without the no-call advice; the starter and checkpoint messages are unchanged.

Three gaps remain in the step-runner model, each failing a step that is valid on a runner with a message that does not name the cause. (a) RUNNER_TEMP is not set (behavior.mjs lines 173-188 set the GITHUB_* files, but not RUNNER_TEMP). A login that writes the password to "$RUNNER_TEMP/registry-password", feeds it to docker login --password-stdin and removes it (ci-runner-temp-file) fails test 6 with "stopped (exit status 1) before docker login ran: .../step.sh: line 1: /registry-password: Read-only file system". RUNNER_TEMP is a documented default variable on every runner. (b) A whole expression inside run, such as if [ "${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}" = true ], becomes the placeholder lab-expression-not-evaluated, so the guard is false and test 6 says only "ran but never called docker login" (ci-guard-expr-compare). README line 118 does say that only the github.event_name, ref and ref_name expressions are filled in, but the message does not say that an expression was replaced, and lab.mjs already has an evaluator for these expressions (evaluate(), RUNS). (c) lab.mjs line 442 always adds "(bash -e stops the step at the first failing command)". That is untrue for a step that timed out: a login followed by sleep 25 gives "exited with status timeout (bash -e stops ...)" (ci-step-timeout). By reading, it is also untrue for shell: sh (sh -e) and for a custom template without -e. All three shapes are off the README path, so the severity is low.
findings.recommendation: Set RUNNER_TEMP (and RUNNER_OS=Linux) to a folder inside the step's temporary directory. For github.* expressions inside run, either fill whole expressions with lab.mjs's evaluate() and the push-to-main context, or, when the script contained a placeholder and docker login never ran, say so in the message. Word the status line from what happened: "did not finish within 20 seconds" for a timeout, and name -e only when the shell command used it. Recheck: ci-runner-temp-file and ci-guard-expr-compare pass, or fail with a message that names the cause; the README form, S9-S10 and S11-S14 are unchanged.
